title: What Service Providers Brought to the Table at ENGAGE 2026
summary: At ENGAGE 2026, mobile and MSO operators shared how trusted, packet-derived data drives autonomous operations, faster 5G troubleshooting, and better subscriber experiences, one proven use case at a time.
body_markdown:
As Thanksgiving approaches, it’s a natural time to reflect on what we’re thankful for, and at NETSCOUT, that list starts with our customers. They trust us with visibility into some of the world’s most critical networks, they push us to keep getting better, and they’re generous about sharing what they’ve learned along the way. That generosity was on full display at this year’s ENGAGE, where a record number of service provider customers took the stage to talk openly about their wins, lessons learned, and even a few hard-earned mistakes so others could benefit.


Across the service provider breakout session track, customers from leading mobile and[cable](https://www.netscout.com/solutions/cable-mso-fixed) operators joined NETSCOUT presenters to share how they are approaching automation,[5G](https://www.netscout.com/solutions/5g) ,[RAN](https://www.netscout.com/solutions/ran-network-solutions) ,[Wi-Fi](https://www.netscout.com/solutions/wireless-voice) , and[AI](https://www.netscout.com/solutions/service-provider-ai-ops) inside their own organizations. The conversations were less about technology for its own sake and more about practical applications including where to start, what to measure, and how to build trust in the data before scaling.


Three themes stood out, offering real-world insights that everyone in the room could learn from.


**The Path to Autonomous Operations**


In “Building the Smartest Self-Optimizing Networks,” NETSCOUT’s[Rick Fulwiler](https://www.netscout.com/blog/author/rick-fulwiler) was joined by two customer panelists, one from a large European operator and one from North America, to discuss what it really takes to move toward autonomous operations. Fulwiler opened the session with a reality check:


- Most operators aim to reach TM Forum Level 4 autonomy by 2030.
- Data readiness remains the biggest barrier.
- Autonomy doesn’t come from simply adding AI on top of existing systems.


That last point set the tone for the rest of the discussion. A mobile voice and data operations leader running thousands of radio sites and hundreds of core network functions put it simply: “Don’t start with AI. Start where value, pain, and readiness meet.”


The European-based operator presented a phased approach built on trusted data, shared context, explainable decisions, and new operating models. The goal was to chip away at the decades of tool sprawl and close the data-readiness gap that Fulwiler introduced. Looking back, the panelist’s biggest lesson was to focus on one important use case and prove its value before moving on. As the panelist put it: “Technology is the easy part. Trust is the hard part.”


The second panelist, a voice and wireless core performance engineering leader from a North American operator, arrived at a similar conclusion: “A self-optimizing network is built one proven use case at a time on data you trust.”


In practice, the panelist revealed how their team uses KPI monitoring, voice experience analytics, and error trending in production. In one case, they compared dropped call rates by region to expose an area that was out of line with the rest of the network. The team traced the root cause to infrastructure, so affected customers got fixes sooner. The panelist’s advice for others on the same path was straightforward: Fix the data first, rank issues by customer impact instead of alarm volume, and standardize before you scale.


Different operators, different starting points, but a unifying message. Autonomy is earned one proven use case at a time, and it starts with data teams can trust.


**Supporting Service Quality at Scale**


Trusted data matters most when service quality is on the line, and that pressure only grows as networks become more complex. “5G Operations with AI-Powered, Cloud-Native Visibility” focused on how NETSCOUT helps carriers troubleshoot faster and protect service quality in[5G standalone](https://www.netscout.com/what-is/5g-sa-vs-nsa) (5G SA) environments, with use cases spanning access and mobility, user plane, Voice over New Radio ([VoNR](https://www.netscout.com/success-stories/5g-voice-services) ), roaming, and[network slicing](https://www.netscout.com/solutions/5g-network-slicing) .


NETSCOUT’s[Claudio Guerrini](https://www.netscout.com/asert/claudio-guerrini) hosted the session, weaving in candid, front-line examples from a principal technical architect on a North American operator’s wireless core team. The team troubleshoots from the customer edge in and prioritizes speed, with a goal of resolving outages in 15 minutes or fewer. That speed was put to the test during a major 5G SA core outage, when[nGeniusONE](https://www.netscout.com/product/ngeniusone-csp) confirmed customer impact within five minutes and helped isolate the failing core function within about 15. The same data turned a top customer complaint into a measurable metric, revealing that calls going straight to voicemail were roughly five times higher in 5G SA than in LTE. That kind of evidence is hard to dispute. As the architect put it: “Nobody ever argues with a NETSCOUT KPI.”


The focus on service quality carried over into “How Data Makes a Difference to AI RAN Outcomes.” The session, led by[Karsten Gaenger](https://www.netscout.com/blog/author/karsten-gaenger) , showed how NETSCOUT’s[RAN-focused sensor, streamer, and Model Concept Protocol (MCP) solutions](https://www.netscout.com/product/omnis-ran-automated-analytics-automated-optimization) let teams ask questions in plain language and get back prioritized issues and recommended actions. That works because the data itself preserves the causality and correlation that traditional KPIs lose.


A network observability manager from a North American operator explained that trust in AI starts with complete, contextual data and clear evidence, and that automation has to be earned gradually. One example made the point. After a configuration change, a 5G slicing customer could not reattach, yet RAN and core KPIs stayed green. Only packet-level session analysis revealed the authentication failures behind the problem. The manager summed up the lesson in one line: “A green dashboard doesn’t always mean a good customer experience.”


**From Data Collection to Actionable Intelligence**


While AI was part of nearly every conversation, many attendees asked where AI was creating value today. NETSCOUT’s Praveen Chandel explored this question for[fixed-line multiple-system operators (MSOs)](https://www.netscout.com/solutions/cable-mso-fixed) as host of “Applying AI-Ready Smart Data in Fixed-Line MSO Networks.” He opened with the common challenge of knowing whether subscribers are actually having a good experience. Packet-derived NETCOUT Smart Data solves that by showing how each subscriber’s experience is performing, session by session, in a form AI agents can query directly. Chandel then turned the stage over to one of NETSCOUT’s cable customers to share how its team monitors subscriber experience today.


A senior manager from the large U.S. operator’s Wi-Fi engineering and data science team explained why visibility matters so much on a hotspot network. As the customer explained, even when the network hits its KPI targets, some customers still say the Wi-Fi is slow.


Outside the home, there is no router to reboot and no call center to call. If the service doesn’t work, customers simply turn off Wi-Fi and switch to cellular, and the operator loses the offload, the session, and any sign that something went wrong. With millions of hotspots and many sessions lasting fewer than 30 seconds, data averaging more than 15 minutes has already missed the moment to triage.


To close that gap, the team enriches NETSCOUT data with device and access point details such as make, model, OS version, and location. This enrichment produces per-client and per-access point (AP) experience scores and lets the team tune each AP to its environment. Next, the team plans to baseline each KPI against its own normal rather than a fleet average. For this team, it all comes back to one principle: “The network is only as good as the experience it delivers.”


**Why Customer Voices Matter**


Product innovation is important, but nothing replaces hearing how real teams put it to work. When customers bring their priorities, challenges, and lessons learned to the table, the conversation shifts from what is possible to what is practical. That is what made these sessions stand out. This Thanksgiving season, we are grateful to the customers who took the stage, shared their experiences, and helped make ENGAGE a place where service providers can learn from one another. There is always room for more at the table, and we look forward to continuing the conversation.


If you attended ENGAGE 2026, you already know the value of these collaborative sessions. If you missed it, now is the time to make plans for next year, and to consider sharing your own insights at the next event.
